name: Physics
notes: The department page writes course codes as PHY / MTH; the registrar catalog this app is built from uses PHYS / MATH, which is the form used here.
At least a 2.0 (C) average in astronomy, physics and mathematics courses must be maintained, and all choices must be approved by the undergraduate physics advisor.
PHYS 141/142/143 (honors) are encouraged for physics majors; the app treats the 12x and 14x introductory sequences as alternatives.

Computer literacy may also be satisfied by a department-approved computing project or by faculty certification instead of a course - those routes cannot be represented as a course requirement, so the course options are modeled and the alternatives noted.
MATH 282 or OPT 287 is 'recommended' for the second advanced-mathematics course; only MATH 281 is stated as required, so the second course is modeled as a choice between the two recommended options.

PHYS 244W (Advanced Experimental Techniques II) and PHYS 256 (Computational Physics) are named on the page but were not scheduled in the harvested 2025-26 terms; they appear in the app as flagged stubs.
Graduate-level courses generally cannot be substituted for undergraduate core requirements.

requirementGroups.label: Pre-concentration: calculus sequence
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One of the following calculus sequences: MTH 161, 162, 164, and 165; MTH 171, 172, 173, and 174

requirementGroups.label: Pre-concentration: introductory physics (3)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Three introductory physics courses: PHY 121: Mechanics or PHY 141: Mechanics (Honors); PHY 122: Electricity and Magnetism or PHY 142; PHY 123: Waves and Modern Physics or PHY 143. PHY 141, 142, and 143 are encouraged for Physics majors.

requirementGroups.label: Core physics courses (6)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: The following six physics courses or their close equivalents: PHY 217: Electricity and Magnetism I; PHY 218: Electricity and Magnetism II; PHY 227: Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics; PHY 235W: Classical Mechanics; PHY 237: Quantum Mechanics of Physical Systems; PHY 246: Quantum Theory

requirementGroups.label: Advanced experimental writing course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One of the following writing courses: PHY 243W: Advanced Experimental Techniques I; PHY 244W: Advanced Experimental Techniques II; PHY 245W: The Advanced Nuclear Science Education Laboratory

requirementGroups.label: One 200-300 level physics or astronomy course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One four-credit 200-300 level physics and/or astronomy course.

requirementGroups.label: Advanced mathematics (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Two courses in advanced mathematics: MTH 281: Applied Boundary Value Problems is required
requirementGroups.note: Only MATH 281 is stated as required; the second course is the group below.

requirementGroups.label: Second advanced mathematics course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: MTH 282: Introduction to Complex Variables with Applications or OPT 287: Mathematical Methods for Optics and Physics is recommended

requirementGroups.label: Computer literacy
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: The computer literacy requirement can be satisfied by: Taking PHY 256: Computational Physics or Taking CSC 171: Intro to Computer Science or Taking CSC 161: Intro to Programming or Completing a computing-based problem approved by the department's undergraduate physics advisor or Having a faculty member certify computer literacy
requirementGroups.note: The non-course routes (approved computing problem, faculty certification) cannot be scheduled and are not modeled.

requirementGroups.label: Natural science outside physics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One course in a natural science other than physics. This can be an astronomy (ASTR) course, or a course outside of the Department of Physics and Astronomy.
requirementGroups.note: Modeled as the natural-science departments outside PHYS; the page allows any course outside the department, which is broader.

upperLevelWriting.label: Upper-level writing within the major
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: PHY 235W: Classical Mechanics ... One of the following writing courses: PHY 243W, PHY 244W, PHY 245W
upperLevelWriting.note: NEEDS VERIFICATION: the page does not state the ULW policy explicitly; modeled as the College's two-course norm satisfied by the major's W-designated courses.
